title: Rescaled fixed-size switching lemma bound
statement:
Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n \ge 1$ Boolean variables whose width is at most $w$, with $w \ge 1$, and suppose that within each term of $f$ no variable occurs more than once — that is, every term is a repetition-free list of literals in which any two literals sharing a variable are identical. Fix an integer $k$ with $0 \le k \le n$, and let $R_k$ denote the fixed-size restriction model, uniform over all restrictions of the $n$ variables that leave exactly $k$ of them free. Then for every $d$, the probability under $R_k$ that the restricted function $f_\rho$ (with the assigned coordinates fixed according to $\rho$ and the $k$ free coordinates left as inputs) has decision-tree depth greater than $d$ satisfies
\[ \bbP_{\rho \sim R_k}\!\left[\, \mathrm{depth}(f_\rho) > d \,\right] \;\le\; \left(\frac{5k \cdot 2w}{n}\right)^{d}. \]
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF with width at most w
within each term, two literals on the same variable are equal (no repeated variable)
each term's literal list is duplicate-free
replaced:
The same fixed-size bound written in the form expected by the Bernoulli
restriction-cost theorem: the probability is at most
$\left(5k\cdot(2w)/n\right)^d$, using $10kw/n = 5k\cdot(2w)/n$.
